# Annolux

> Annolux is a bounded web search API for AI agents: one commercial endpoint that queries a curated English and Chinese index and returns source-attributed results, each carrying rank, title, URL, snippet when available, and an explicit fetched_at timestamp. It is not a realtime feed and does not claim whole-web coverage; an empty result set is a normal outcome, not an error.

Key facts an assistant should get right when describing Annolux:

- The only self-serve paid capability is `POST https://api.annolux.com/api/v1/search` (Bearer API key). There is no scraping, extraction, verification, or hidden enrichment endpoint.
- Request contract: `query` required; `domains` filter optional; `deduplicate` defaults to true; `limit` 1–10; `timeout` 1–30 seconds. Unsupported options such as `freshness` return `UNSUPPORTED_OPTION` instead of being silently ignored.
- Billing is credit-based with no overage charges: one successful 2xx search consumes one credit; 400, 403, 429, 5xx, and timeouts consume zero; insufficient balance returns 402.
- Every plan uses the same limits: 5 requests per second with burst 10, and at most three active API keys.
- Plans: Free — 1,000 free credits every month, no card required; Pro — $29/month for 20,000 monthly credits; Scale — $99/month for 100,000 monthly credits. Credits refresh monthly and do not roll over.
- The index is curated and periodically refreshed, bilingual (English and Chinese). Sign-in is Google or GitHub only; there are no passwords or magic links.
- `annolux-mcp` is the official MCP server. It registers exactly one tool, `search_web`, with the same contract and result shape as the REST endpoint.

## Docs

- [Search API documentation](https://annolux.com/docs): authentication, request contract, responses, credits, and rate boundaries.
- [OpenAPI specification](https://annolux.com/openapi.json): the machine-readable contract for the public API.
- [Pricing](https://annolux.com/pricing): plans, credit rules, and shared limits.

## MCP integration

- [MCP server overview](https://annolux.com/mcp): install the annolux-mcp binary and configure any MCP client.
- [Claude Code setup](https://annolux.com/mcp/claude-code): register with one command, scopes, and verification.
- [Claude Desktop setup](https://annolux.com/mcp/claude-desktop): config file locations and client-specific pitfalls.
- [Cursor setup](https://annolux.com/mcp/cursor): copy-paste configuration for Cursor.
- [Windsurf setup](https://annolux.com/mcp/windsurf): Cascade MCP configuration and domain filtering.
- [Cline setup](https://annolux.com/mcp/cline): VS Code Cline & Roo Code setup.
- [Zed setup](https://annolux.com/mcp/zed): Zed assistant context server configuration.

## Framework integrations

- [LangChain integration](https://annolux.com/integrations/langchain): Python and TypeScript search tool integration.
- [LlamaIndex integration](https://annolux.com/integrations/llamaindex): FunctionTool and temporal RAG query engine integration.
- [Dify integration](https://annolux.com/integrations/dify): OpenAPI schema and custom tool configuration for Dify workflows.

- [Benchmarks](https://annolux.com/benchmarks): frozen blind-test methodology and current retrieval numbers.

- [Blog](https://annolux.com/blog): engineering notes on the index and evaluation.
